subject: Hosted evaluation: quickstart endpoints, rate plan, and prefix/KV cache follow-up
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@cartwheellabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elaine Park <elaine.park@cartwheellabs.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jun 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Demo today — hosted evaluation & quickstart asks

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the demo this morning. Really helpful to see Redwood's serving runtime and the routing examples. Elaine and I pulled together a short list of follow-up items so we can scope a hosted evaluation: 

- Workload profile: chat + embeddings. Expectation is ~250–350 rps at peak (spikey) across two endpoints (chat-stream and embed-sync); average prompt ~50–70 tokens, average response ~60–100 tokens.
- SLOs: target p95 latency < 350ms for chat-stream (we'd accept occasional spikes during peak).
- Test data: attached a quick requirements spreadsheet with expected daily active users and token estimates.

Primary asks for quickstart:
1) Can you provision a staging sandbox (isolated API key + staging endpoints) for Cartwheel for ~2 weeks? We want to run a soak and a small synthetic replay.
2) What are the hosted default rate limits (requests/sec and tokens/min)? How do burst policies work?
3) Does the hosted API support prefix/KV caching (we have many repeated prompt prefixes across customers)? If so, what's the recommended TTL and configuration approach?
4) If we exceed default limits during evaluation, can you provide temporary bump/burst capacity or should we consider Dedicated? What are the thresholds?

Next steps from our side: Elaine will share SSO requirements and our security checklist. Can you share a sample quickstart and the basic endpoint mapping you recommend for chat vs embeddings?

Attaching: cartwheel_requirements.xlsx (high-level traffic).

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alex

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Demo today — hosted evaluation & quickstart asks

Alex / Elaine —

Great to meet you both — thanks for the clear requirements doc. Below is a concise plan and answers to the quick questions so your team can evaluate hosted suitability quickly.

Quickstart plan (proposed):
- 2-week hosted evaluation in a sandbox workspace (isolated API keys + telemetry) — we'll provide a staging base URL and a single sandbox API key to start.
- Endpoint mapping recommendation: 
  * /v1/chat-stream -> streaming chat endpoint (best for low-latency user-facing chat).
  * /v1/embeddings -> synchronous embeddings endpoint (batch-friendly).
- Rate plan (default hosted):
  * Default per-key baseline: 60 requests/min and 60k tokens/min (configurable).
  * Burst policy: short bursts up to 3x baseline for up to 1 minute when capacity available; sustained increases require a temporary bump request.
  * For your stated peak (250–350 rps), the hosted baseline is insufficient; we recommend either a temporary burst bump for the sandbox or scoped Dedicated capacity.
- Prefix/KV caching: supported. We have two caching layers: prefix caching (automatic detection on repeated prefixes) and an explicit KV cache you can populate via the API. Recommended starter config: prefix TTL 2h, KV cache window 30m for conversational contexts; we can tune further based on replay results.

Immediate next steps I can do this week:
1) Provision sandbox endpoints + initial API key (I'll need a short legal & security contact to sign off on the evaluation).
2) Share the Redwood hosted quickstart PDF (attached) with sample curl commands and an example prefix-caching config snippet.
3) Loop in Soojin and Aditya to confirm rate bump options and provide a rateplan matrix for your projected traffic.

Can you confirm: (a) which dataset you'll replay for the soak (sample size), and (b) the security contact for SSO/KMS questions? Once we have that I'll start onboarding and request a temporary bump for the first 48 hours of the soak.

Best,
Marissa

Marissa / Aditya —

Quick technical notes from infra/runtime side after reviewing Cartwheel's traffic sheet:

- Baseline we advertise is intentionally conservative; we can lift sandbox keys to a temporary higher bucket to support replay. Proposal for sandbox soak:
  * Sandbox bump (48 hrs): 1,200 requests/min and 1,200k tokens/min (engine-backed throttles will enforce total throughput across the workspace).
  * Sustained hosted target: we can run a multi-worker setup but for production-level 250–350 rps you should evaluate Dedicated — otherwise costs and noisy-neighbor risk increase.
- Burst semantics: token-based enforcement. If cumulative tokens/min exceeds the assigned quota, we reject further requests with 429 until the next window. We can also provide a soft-throttle header X-Redwood-Backoff to help clients implement client-side backoff.
- Caching: prefix caching is enabled at the serving layer; TTLs are tunable per-key via the control plane. For your workload I recommend: prefix TTL 2h, KV cache TTL 20–40m depending on session churn. We'll provide a sample control-plane config that Cartwheel can apply.
- Staging endpoints: will be created under a temporary hostname (staging-api.redwood.com/cl-9876/*). We'll include a staging webhook for logs (to your secure S3) if you want live trace ingestion.

I'll attach the rateplan matrix to this thread. Marissa, if you want I can propose the exact uplift numbers and the flow to request the temporary bump so Alex's team can proceed with the replay tomorrow.

—Soojin
